name: Madagascar (Malagasy kingdoms and state)
summary: The island settled by Austronesian sailors from Borneo and by Africans, where kingdoms such as Merina united much of the island before French colonisation (1896). Independent since 1960.

knownFor.label: Royal Hill of Ambohimanga
knownFor.note: Sacred hill of the Merina kings, a World Heritage Site.

knownFor.label: Lamba
knownFor.note: A wrapped cloth worn by Malagasy people.

knownFor.label: Vanilla
knownFor.note: Madagascar grows most of the world’s vanilla.

location.value: An island in the Indian Ocean off south-east Africa; the world’s fourth-largest island.

terrain.value: A steep eastern escarpment with lowland forest, central highlands at 750–1,500 m, and drier land sloping west to the Mozambique Channel.

climate.value: Tropical to subtropical: a hot rainy season (November–April) with destructive cyclones and a cooler dry season; semi-arid in the south-west.

resources.value: Rice, zebu cattle, vanilla (80% of the world’s natural vanilla), cloves and unique wildlife (over 90% endemic).

disasters.value: Cyclones (Gafilo in 2004 was the strongest recorded) and droughts such as the 2021–2022 famine.

disease.value: Plague outbreaks in 2014 and 2017, and a measles outbreak in 2019.

migration.value: Settled by Austronesians from present-day Indonesia (by about 500–700 CE), joined by Bantu groups from East Africa around the 9th century.

tradeRoutes.value: Arab traders arrived between the 7th and 9th centuries; Swahili-speaking Antalaotra controlled Indian Ocean trade on the north-west coast.

wealth.value: A least-developed country; about 80% of people lived in poverty in 2025.

inequality.value: Nobles (Andriana), commoners (Hova) and slaves in the Merina kingdom; slavery was abolished in 1896.

governmentType.value: Kingdoms (Merina, Sakalava), then a French colony, then a republic.

keyRulers.value: Andrianampoinimerina (reunited Imerina in the 1790s). Radama I (1810–28). Queen Ranavalona I (1828–61). Philibert Tsiranana (1960–72).

succession.value: Royal succession; elections and coups since 1960.

institutions.value: The Merina kingdom’s royal court and laws.

stability.value: Political crises: protests ended the First Republic in 1972, a standoff in 2002, and coups in 2009 and 2025.

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between highland and coastal groups.

armyAndTech.value: Radama I gained British military and financial help through an 1817 treaty; British advisers later trained the army.

majorWars.value: The French conquest (1895), the Menalamba rebellion (1895–97) and the Malagasy Uprising of 1947.

territoryChange.value: Merina kings unified most of the island; Radama I controlled two-thirds of it by 1828.

alliancesRivals.value: A treaty with Britain (1817); rivalry with France, which annexed the island in 1896.

scienceEducation.value: Missionaries arriving from 1818 opened schools, wrote Malagasy in the Roman alphabet and translated the Bible.

communicationTransport.value: Outrigger canoes carried the first settlers; under French rule, forced labour built a railway and roads linking coastal cities to Antananarivo.

religion.value: Christianity is predominant; many still honour ancestors, for example with the famadihana reburial.

languageWriting.value: Malagasy, which comes from the Southeast Barito languages of Borneo, and French.

artsArchitecture.value: Silk weaving and the lamba national dress; the valiha bamboo zither; elaborate tombs.

socialStructure.value: The Malagasy form over 90% of people, in 18 subgroups; the Merina are the largest (about 26%).

sharedIdentity.value: A shared Malagasy language and ancestor traditions.

dailyLife.value: Rice is eaten at every meal; zebu cattle are a sign of wealth.

neighbours.value: Mozambique (the nearest mainland), Comoros, Mayotte, Réunion and Mauritius.

riseSignals.value: Unification under the Merina kings from the 1790s.

peakPeriod.value: Merina power in the early 19th century.
